body:
Dear ASVS Leaders and Working Group,

@jmanico @danielcuthbert @elarlang @ImanSharaf @meghanjacquot @EnigmaRosa @csfreak92 @ryarmst @TobiasAhnoff @randomstuff @cronchie

I wanted to make sure everyone is updated as to the current plan as it was pointed out to me that our communications have not been as clear as they could have been.

### tl;dr

We announced a release candidate on 31st March, we are gathering and actioning extensive feedback now and I want to release a final version of 5.0 before OWASP AppSec EU Barcelona on May 29th/30th.

If you have strong objections to this, please read the full details I have included and then comment below. Alternatively if you are ok with this, you can just thumbs-up this message 😃 

### Details

Towards the end of last year at the working group call and then at the summit in November, I expressed my belief that we were nearly ready for a release candidate and then a release. Whilst the timings have slipped slightly, we have still followed that goal with a release candidate being publicized on 31st March 2025.

The ASVS in its current form has been a work in progress since before 4.0.3, it has had many eyes on it over these ~4 years and has had many refinements made. Pretty much every single 4.0.3 requirement has been modified with the aim of improving it and we also have many new requirements.

The project summit last November was a particular boost with eight of us getting together in person (plus some very active remote participants), including both newer and more established contributors.

I feel highly confident that we are the stage where a new release is not only desirable but in fact critical for the continuing success of the project.

One the one hand, we have a comprehensively reviewed, revamped, and improved set of requirements that provides a significant uplift to version 4.x. I am not going to pretend that the release will be perfect but clearly no previous release has been perfect. Instead, I  believe that our goal should be to get a release that is "good enough" and then see where we progress from there.

One the other hand, it has been too long since a formal release. ASVS 4.0.1 (last major release) was released in March 2019 and ASVS 4.0.3 (last minor release) was released in October 2021. we risk the ASVS becoming irrelevant if we cannot release stable versions in a timely fashion. We have been building momentum for this release since last summer and if we do not go ahead with this release, I think we are likely to lose that momentum entirely.

I have therefore proposed the OWASP AppSec EU conference in Barcelona (29th/30th May) as the venue for this new release and, with my encouragement, Elar is scheduled to speak about ASVS, ideally to announce the new release.

Certainly a 5.0 release is not the end of the road and we can immediately start thinking about what refinements we would like to see in a 5.0.1 or 5.1 version but a release will allow us a solid base to continue and also allow for the growth of extension projects such as an ASVS testing guide or more detailed developer guidance.

If having read all of this, you feel that we should not release by the end of May, please let me know your thoughts below. Otherwise, I'd appreciate a thumbs up on this post.

comments.body:
> Certainly a 5.0 release is not the end of the road and we can immediately start thinking about what refinements we would like to see in a 5.0.1 or 5.1 version but a release will allow us a solid base to continue and also allow for the growth of extension projects such as an ASVS testing guide or more detailed developer guidance.

So much this. It's vital we get this into hands of practitioners so they can use it, find out what works, what doesnt and give us feedback.
I am in agreement. There will always be more we can do.

I have stated reservations about releasing next month but after listening to the wishes of the ASVS leadership community, I 100% support pushing to make sure we release in May. 

I'll shift gears around suggesting big changes and will work more towards getting the release out.

Thank you @danielcuthbert @ryarmst @elarlang and @tghosth
